note: On starting point he is close to the ideal case. At 5'10" and 172.7 lb his BMI is in the normal range, his diet is already dialled in, he trains three times a week and walks 7,000-8,000 steps, and the goal is tone, strength and muscle rather than rescue — good-to-great almost verbatim. Health had genuinely been the neglected corner for decades and is not a crisis: high cholesterol managed with a cardiologist, an A1C he pulled back out of the pre-diabetic range himself with a glucose monitor. He fails the commercial half. An MRI technologist is a licensed healthcare professional but not a business owner or physician in the sense the stated ICP means, and income fails on the prospect's own words — 'it's a bit steep for my pocket' and 'the sticker price, it was a little shock to me.' This one is worth reading alongside the observation that income screening may filter out deals a payment plan could carry, with the twist that here no payment plan was offered at all, so the hypothesis was never tested.
